text:
Alex: quick idea — instead of hard reserved slots for Dedicated GPU pools, what if we use short-lived "soft leases" backed by a token-envelope per tenant?
Mira: can you sketch what a "soft lease" buys you vs current reservation?
Alex: sure. soft lease = capacity hint + preemption window. you get a token budget that refills, allowing bursts without permanently pinning GPUs. if preempted, caller gets a controlled failure or fallback to a cheaper model variant. cheaper than burning reserved nodes.
Sanjay: sounds promising. how do we prevent noisy neighbors from draining tokens? fairness?
Alex: token envelope per-tenant + bucket refill rate tied to committed capacity. policy example (pseudo-DSL):
```
policy {
  tenant: "acme"
  qos: "prod"
  lease_type: "soft"
  duration_s: 60
  tokens_per_sec: 4
  burst_tokens: 32
  preemptible: true
}
```
Sanjay: i like the simplicity. token semantics = number of allowed concurrent requests or some normalized unit (gpu-seconds)? which do we use?
Mira: normalized to amortized GPU-seconds makes more sense for cost accounting. map request cost = seq_len * tokens * model_cost_factor.
Lia: operational concerns: what signals will trigger preemption? p95 latency over SLA, GPU queue length, and low cache hit rate?
Alex: yes — primary triggers: p95 latency > target, queue depth > X, or sustained GPU util > 95%. fallback order: 1) steer to cached result (if applicable), 2) route to smaller model variant, 3) evict soft lease.
Ben: how do we surface this in control plane? operator boundary question: scheduler decides eviction; operator reconciler exposes per-tenant envelopes and refill rates. need a clear API so Dedicated customers can bind a commit -> refill-rate mapping.
Mira: agreed. also need safety limits: min-reservation floor for critical tenants (non-preemptible), plus global throttles so we don't oscillate.
Sanjay: persistence: if the token ledger is in-memory and we crash, tenants could get infinite burst after restart. we need a small durable ledger or leaky-bucket that persists last refill timestamp.
Ben: we can implement a compact ledger in the control-plane DB: store last_tokens and last_ts per tenant. cheap reads/writes.
Alex: rollout plan: 1) implement token-envelope service + simple admission hook, 2) opt-in on a subset of tenants, 3) add predictive smoothing (short ML model) to pre-warm envelopes, 4) promote to default.
Lia: observability: expose per-tenant token usage, eviction events, fallback counts, and cost delta. alert on sudden token exhaustion spikes.
Mira: small nit — need clear SLA messaging to customers: soft leases can be preempted during congestion. they must provide fallback behavior.
ops-bot: deploy triggered: feature/token-envelope v0.1 -> staging (build 4021) :rocket:
Alex: action items: (1) Sanjay to mock ledger schema, (2) Ben to draft control-plane API contract, (3) Mira/Lia to propose SLO triggers and dashboard, (4) I'll write a short RFC with the DSL and rollout plan.
Sanjay: I'll paste a quick ledger proto later today.
Ben: ack. will draft API and share by EOD tomorrow.
Mira: thanks — this feels much more cost-friendly than adding more reserved capacity for bursty tenants. :thumbsup:
Alex: cool. if nobody objects i'll start the RFC tomorrow.
